purpose: Maps business findings to the economic question they raise. Findings explain scenario assumptions. They never map mechanically into an exit outcome.

sensitivityRules.numeric: A numeric financing, dilution or discount assumption needs cited evidence ids that exist and are not unavailable or conflicting, or an explicit user-estimate flag set by the user. Weak evidence yields a qualitative sensitivity only.
sensitivityRules.userEstimate: Only a user-supplied value may carry the user-estimate flag. A model proposal never does.

rows.requiredEconomicQuestion: Does the growth/exit case depend on retention improvement that has not occurred?
evidenceNeeded: cohort or customer retention with period and denominator
evidence of repeat use, renewal or expansion
stated demand evidence and who pays
rows.stageNotes: Before product-market fit, absent retention history is unknown, never a retention value of zero. Record it as missing evidence and keep the growth question open.

rows.requiredEconomicQuestion: What happens to growth and funding needs if acquisition becomes less efficient?
evidenceNeeded: share of growth from paid or single-channel acquisition
acquisition cost trend over dated periods
organic or referral share

rows.businessFinding: Weak contribution economics or long payback
rows.requiredEconomicQuestion: What financing and dilution are needed before growth becomes self-funding?
evidenceNeeded: contribution margin or gross margin with period
payback period or an explicit statement it cannot yet be measured
unit-level cost and revenue definition

rows.requiredEconomicQuestion: Test financing, dilution, employment interruption and exercise-funding pressure together.
evidenceNeeded: cash or runway statement with date
recent burn
financing plan or lender and investor commitments
rows.note: Employment loss and equity decline are correlated exposures. Do not multiply them as independent risks.

rows.businessFinding: Strong business at a demanding valuation
rows.requiredEconomicQuestion: Does plausible business success still produce employee common-share upside?
evidenceNeeded: last priced round or valuation, with date and source
preference stack or capitalization if available
plausible exit routes and their scale
rows.note: Business strength and common-equity upside are separate judgments. A strong business can still offer little to common holders at a demanding price.

rows.requiredEconomicQuestion: Withhold a definitive common payout; use explicit bounded/externally supplied scenarios.
evidenceNeeded: liquidation preferences and participation terms
outstanding debt, warrants or structured instruments
source of each term

rows.requiredEconomicQuestion: Show uncertainty and financing sensitivities; do not substitute mature-company metrics.
evidenceNeeded: team and technical or market evidence appropriate to the stage
funding history and milestones
what would count as the next proof point
